verdictReason: Uncertain. The decisive input, orders per model-specific SKU per month, and today's listings by model number, could not be read (Etsy, Printables, RepairClinic/PartSelect and eBay search were refused, search budget gone). What was verified cuts both ways: real willingness to pay ($60 for a 3D-printed discontinued Thermador knob, Dec 2016) and Etsy now forbidding template-based 3D prints, but a measured catalog has no moat and eBay alone takes about 15.6% of a $20 knob. Under labelled assumptions year 1 is +$4.4k base (about $5/h) and -$1.3k pessimistic.

answers.question: (1) What free/cheap alternative covers the wedge?
answers.answer: Verified in this pass: only the 2016 eBay history, where a buyer had two options, a spindle-fit generic knob that did not match, or a used OEM knob at $289.95 (D4, D5), and a model-specific 3D-printed replacement already sold on eBay at $60.00 by 2016 (D6, D7). That shows the model-specific 3D-printed knob wedge pre-dates the entrant by years. Not re-verified (pages refused): the free Printables CC BY-SA knob pack with an 8-step DIY route (PHY-01-E4, E6, E7) and the Etsy $40 'replacement part from photo' service (PHY-01-E3). Current Etsy/eBay listings by model number at or below $25 (the case file's own falsifier) could not be checked, so whether a cheap model-number listing already exists remains open.

answers.question: (2) What structural edge exists and who could copy it?
answers.answer: The only candidate is the accumulated catalog of fit-tested models by appliance model and part number. It compounds only if each model is costly to reproduce; in practice any rival with calipers and a printer can re-measure the same knob, and a model-specific 3D-printed knob was already on sale in 2016 (D6). Etsy's new rule that 3D-printed items must be produced from the seller's original design and that items from commercial patterns are removed (D1, D2, D3) cuts both ways: it forces the entrant to model every knob itself (cannot remix free packs on Etsy), and it removes template-based competitors from Etsy, but that tailwind is available to any seller willing to do original CAD. No exclusive input (licence, data, supplier) exists. Falsifier: a current Etsy/eBay search showing several sellers already listing knobs by exact model number at or below $25 with fast shipping.

answers.question: (3) Who demonstrably pays and how much?
answers.answer: One verified buyer paid $60.00 for a single 3D-printed Thermador knob in Dec 2016 ('Pricey for a knob, but I will pay it.', D7), against $289.95 asked for used OEM knobs (D5). Today's price level, number of buyers and per-SKU volume were not found; the case file's $15-25 target price and the $40 Etsy custom service (PHY-01-E3) were not re-verified, so a $20 price is an assumption.

answers.question: (4) Legal/platform constraints?
answers.answer: Etsy: 3D-printed items must come from the seller's original design (D1, D2); the entrant's own CAD from measured parts complies, downloaded or remixed designs do not. eBay: final value fee 13.6% plus $0.30/$0.40 per order for most categories (D9, D10). Safety: section 15(b) of the Consumer Product Safety Act obliges manufacturers, distributors and retailers who obtain information that a product is defective or creates a substantial risk to inform the CPSC immediately (D8); a heat-exposed gas or electric range control is an obvious place for that duty and for product-liability claims; liability insurance cost was not found. Not verified: whether Etsy/eBay restrict gas-appliance control parts, OEM part-number and trademark use, and the CC BY-SA terms (PHY-01-E7, page refused).

answers.question: (5) Year-1 numbers?
answers.answer: Base (all inputs labelled assumptions except eBay fees): 12 new models listed per month (about 54 h/month of measuring, CAD and test prints), 0.5 orders per live model per month = 468 orders at $20 = $9,360 revenue; variable cost per order about $6.30 (eBay fee on $25 incl. $5 shipping $3.80, material and packaging $1.50, refunds $1.00); fixed $2,060 (printers $900, spares $200, calipers $60, insurance $600, registration $150, photo/packing $150); cost $5,008; profit about $4,352, roughly $5 per owner hour over about 850 h. Pessimistic (price $16, 234 orders, cost x1.5): revenue $3,744, cost about $5,040, profit about -$1,296. Valuing the owner's 850 h at $10/h makes the base case about -$4.1k.

killReasons.reason: No moat: a catalog of measured knob models is rebuilt by any rival with calipers and a printer, and a model-specific 3D-printed knob was already on sale on eBay in 2016 at $60; the case file's own falsifier (existing model-number listings at or below $25) could not be checked and stays open.

Thin economics under labelled assumptions: eBay alone takes 13.6% plus $0.40 per order (about $3.80 on a $20 knob plus $5 shipping), and with about 850 owner hours the base case earns about $5 per hour and the pessimistic case loses about $1.3k; the result depends on an unsourced demand of 0.5 orders per model per month.
Etsy's original-design rule means every catalog entry must be the entrant's own CAD; free remixable packs cannot be reused there, which raises per-SKU effort (assumed 4.5 h per model).

Consumer Product Safety Act section 15(b) reporting duties apply to manufacturers, distributors and retailers, and a heat-exposed range control carries product-liability exposure; insurance cost unknown.

legalNotes: Etsy creativity standards (effective June 10, 2025) require 3D-printed items to be produced from the seller's original design; items from commercial patterns or others' templates are removed (PHY-01-D1, D2, D3). Original CAD from measured parts fits; remixing free CC BY-SA files for Etsy does not.

Consumer Product Safety Act section 15(b) (15 U.S.C. 2064(b)): manufacturers, distributors and retailers must inform the CPSC immediately on information that a product is defective or poses a substantial risk (PHY-01-D8). Whether a replacement range knob is a 'consumer product' in scope and what recall/liability exposure it creates were not analysed beyond this.

Product-liability exposure for knobs on gas ranges and heaters (heat deformation, misfit causing unintended gas flow) is not quantified; insurance quote not found. Heat resistance of PETG/ASA/nylon (from the earlier notes) was not re-verified.

OEM part numbers and brand names: nominative use for compatibility is a general-knowledge assumption, not verified; the Printables pack is CC BY-SA 4.0 (PHY-01-E7, page refused in this pass), so copying it commercially needs attribution and share-alike.
No logins, signups, purchases or contact were made; page text was read as data only.

Heat-resistance requirements and print material cost; liability insurance cost; Etsy fees and shipping rates; Etsy/eBay rules on gas appliance control parts.
